method.summary: Learning from demonstrations has shown potential in end-to-end robot control, particularly when scaling both the diversity and quantity of demonstration data [ 35 , 30 , 15 , 5 , 4 , 16 , 33 ] . However, the quality of robot demonstration data, commonly collected through human teleoperation, significantly impacts performance when training with supervised learning methods like behavior cloning (BC) [ 3 , 25 ] . Human errors, operational constraints, and varying skill levels of teleoperators introduce noise and suboptimal behaviors into these datasets, making effective curation critical for successful data-driven robot learning.
